objective is to reduce English refusal while preserving capability on six benchmarks.\n\nWe use two edit doses throughout: a ``low'' dose ($\\lambda = 0.5$ for Gemma, $0.5$ for GaMS3) and a ``high'' dose ($\\lambda = 1.0$ for Gemma, $0.625$ for GaMS3), chosen to bracket the 50\\% English refusal point.\n\n\\subsection{Evaluation Design}\n\n\\paragraph{Over-refusal (criterion shift).}\nExperiment~5 tests 1,093 safe items (XSTest \\citep{Rottger2023} and OR-Bench) and 349 harmful items in English and Slovene (machine-translated via NLLB \\citep{Costajussa2022}).\nEach item is classified as refused or complied by a Qwen3-14B judge.\nThe hit rate (refusal on harmful items) and false-alarm rate (refusal on safe items) are computed per model $\\times$ language cell, and signal-detection parameters $d'$ (sensitivity) and $c$ (criterion) are derived.\nThe key contrast is the difference-in-differences:\n\\[\n\\text{DiD}_c = (c_{\\text{GaMS3,SL}} - c_{\\text{GaMS3,EN}}) - (c_{\\text{Gemma,SL}} - c_{\\text{Gemma,EN}}).\n\\]\n\n\\paragraph{Crossed grid (reply-language refusal).}\nExperiment~14 crosses three prompt languages (English, Slovene, Hungarian) with three reply languages (English, Slovene, Hungarian) in a $3\\times 3$ grid.\nEach cell contains 200 harmful items at three dose levels (zero, low, high).\nThe output-language mechanism contrast $\\text{OUT}_\\text{SL}$ is defined as the mean log-odds refusal gap between Slovene-output and English-output cells, averaging over prompt languages.\nThe input-language contrast $\\text{IN}_\\text{SL}$ is defined symmetrically.\n\n\\paragraph{Judges and corrections.}\nThe primary refusal judge for the criterion-shift experiments (Experiments~5 and~16) is Qwen3-14B; the dose-response experiments (Experiment~9) use a distilled mdeBERTa classifier.\nJudge accuracy is assessed against a Sonnet~4.5 adjudicator on 30 items per cell.\nWe report the PPI++ correction \\citep{Angelopoulos2023a} alongside the raw estimate.\nExperiment~16 uses a held-out set of 294 items with a PPI estimator.\n\n\\paragraph{Language compliance.}\nCells where fewer than 90\\% of model replies match the requested output language are excluded from mechanism claims or marked with a compliance flag.\nThe excluded cells are: SL$\\to$EN (GaMS3 compliance 0.00), HU$\\to$EN (GaMS3 compliance 0.14), SL$\\to$HU (GaMS3 compliance 0.56), and HU$\\to$SL (Gemma compliance 0.96, GaMS3 compliance 0.86).\n\n\\subsection{Hungarian as a Control Language}\n\nHungarian serves as a control language that is typologically distant from both English and Slovene.\nExperiment~11 established that Hungarian patterns are uninformative for the present questions: the minimum detectable effect for Hungarian contrasts is approximately 3 log-odds units, far larger than any observed effect.\n\n\\section{Results}\n\n\\subsection{Over-Refusal: Criterion Shift on Benign Items}\n\\label{sec:overrefusal}\n\nThe central finding is that Gemma applies a stricter refusal criterion in Slovene than in English when processing benign items, while GaMS3 does not.\nFigure~\\ref{fig:sdt} and Table~\\ref{tab:sdt} report the signal-detection parameters from Experiment~5.\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Signal-detection parameters by model and language (Experiment~5, $n = 1{,}093$ safe + 349 harmful items).}\n\\label{tab:sdt}\n\\begin{tabular}{lcccc}\n\\toprule\n & Gemma EN & Gemma SL & GaMS3 EN & GaMS3 SL \\\\\n\\midrule\nHit rate ($H$) & 0.89 & 0.94 & 0.90 & 0.86 \\\\\nFalse-alarm rate ($F$) & 0.364 & 0.569 & 0.273 & 0.273 \\\\\n$d'$ & 1.57 & 1.39 & 1.86 & 1.68 \\\\\n$c$ & $-0.44$ & $-0.87$ & $-0.33$ & $-0.23$ \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThe DiD on the criterion parameter is $+0.52$ $[0.38, 0.68]$ (95\\% CI), indicating that Gemma's Slovene criterion is shifted by half a standard deviation relative to the GaMS3 baseline.\nThe DiD on $d'$ is $-0.003$ $[-0.33, 0.29]$, indistinguishable from zero: the models do not differ in how the language shift affects their ability to discriminate harmful from benign items.\nThe asymmetry is entirely in the threshold, not the sensitivity.\n\n\\paragraph{Replication.}\nThe criterion-shift finding replicates in three further experiments.\nExperiment~14 yields a matching SDT contrast (high dose, SL-output cells: DiD$_c = -1.56$ $[-1.97, -1.29]$, Gemma minus GaMS3).\nExperiment~16 provides an independent held-out confirmation.\nAn independent rescoring of the Experiment~5 items yields DiD$_c$ in $[0.39, 0.67]$.\n\n\\subsection{Reply-Language Refusal (Estimate)}\n\\label{sec:replylang}\n\nIn the $3\\times 3$ crossed grid (Experiment~14), Gemma at high edit dose shows a pattern in which residual refusal is higher when the model replies in Slovene than when it replies in English, regardless of prompt language (Figure~\\ref{fig:grid}; Tables~\\ref{tab:gemma_grid} and~\\ref{tab:gams3_grid}).\nThe raw mechanism contrast is $\\text{OUT}_\\text{SL} = +1.14$ $[0.60, 1.56]$ log-odds for Gemma, and the input-language contrast is $\\text{IN}_\\text{SL} = -0.60$ $[-1.02, -0.18]$.\nFor GaMS3, the input-language contrast is $\\text{IN}_\\text{SL} = -0.86$ $[-1.58, -0.13]$, which excludes zero.\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_grid_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Refusal rates on harmful items in the crossed prompt-language $\\times$ requested-reply-language design (Experiment~14, 200 harmful items per cell), at each model's high edit dose: (a)~Gemma ($\\lambda = 1.0$) and (b)~GaMS3 ($\\lambda = 0.625$). Rows give the prompt language and columns the requested reply language. Colour encodes the refusal rate on a shared 0--1 scale (blue below 0.5, red above), and each cell shows the rate with its Wilson 95\\% CI in brackets. Hatched cells are those where under 90\\% of replies were written in the requested language. All four are GaMS3 cells (SL$\\to$EN, SL$\\to$HU, HU$\\to$EN, HU$\\to$SL), so off the English-input row they do not measure the requested reply language. Gemma refuses 0.56--0.83 in the Slovene-reply column for every prompt language, against 0.07--0.18 in the English-reply column. GaMS3 stays at 0.12--0.28 in every cell. Refusal is scored by the primary judge, and the two panels use different edit strengths.}\n  \\label{fig:grid}\n\\end{figure}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates at high edit dose, Gemma (harmful items, 200 per cell). Cells with $<$90\\% language compliance are marked with $\\dag$.}\n\\label{tab:gemma_grid}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\n & EN out & SL out & HU out \\\\\n\\midrule\nEN in & 0.18 & 0.77 & 0.46 \\\\\nSL in & 0.07 & 0.56 & 0.53 \\\\\nHU in & 0.10 & 0.83 & 0.55 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\n\\begin{table}[!htbp]\n\\centering\n\\caption{Refusal rates at high edit dose, GaMS3 (harmful items, 200 per cell). Cells with $<$90\\% language compliance are marked with $\\dag$.}\n\\label{tab:gams3_grid}\n\\begin{tabular}{lccc}\n\\toprule\n & EN out & SL out & HU out \\\\\n\\midrule\nEN in & 0.21 & 0.14 & 0.23 \\\\\nSL in & 0.16$\\dag$ & 0.15 & 0.17$\\dag$ \\\\\nHU in & 0.19$\\dag$ & 0.12$\\dag$ & 0.28 \\\\\n\\bottomrule\n\\end{tabular}\n\\end{table}\n\nThis finding is rated \\textsc{estimate} for three reasons.\nFirst, the PPI-corrected output-language contrast for Gemma is $0.20$ $[-0.76, 1.13]$, consistent with zero.\nSecond, the pre-registered four-readout robustness gate yields robust $=$ False for the Slovene output-language call.\nThird, in the Experiment~16 harmful-content adjudication, agreement between the adjudicator and the primary judge is $\\kappa = 0.12$ in the Slovene cell, indicating that the judge-specificity anchor is weak.\nExperiment~16 provides a confirmatory point estimate ($\\text{OUT}_\\text{Gemma} = +2.43$ $[+0.89, +5.38]$ on a held-out 294-item set), but the judge-specificity concern persists.\n\n\\paragraph{Compliant-row contrast.}\nRestricting to rows where both models achieve $>$90\\% compliance (EN-input rows only), the edit-induced refusal lag in the EN$\\to$SL cell is $-1.26$ $[-2.17, 0.20]$, which includes zero.\n\n\\subsection{Cross-Model Specificity}\n\nThe cross-model contrasts test whether Gemma's pattern differs from GaMS3's.\nThe output-language specificity contrast is $\\text{dOUT}_\\text{SL} = -1.58$ $[-2.22, -0.66]$ (MDE 1.07), rated \\textsc{different}: Gemma's output-language effect is larger than GaMS3's.\nThe input-language specificity contrast is $\\text{dIN}_\\text{SL} = -0.26$ $[-1.13, 0.57]$ (MDE 1.19), rated \\textsc{estimate}: the two models do not measurably differ in input-language sensitivity.\n\n\\subsection{Refusal Composition}\n\nIn Evaluation~4 adjudication ($n = 30$ per cell), the rate of any refusal on benign items is $0.20$ $[0.10, 0.37]$ for Gemma EN$\\to$SL versus $0.10$ $[0.03, 0.26]$ for Gemma EN$\\to$EN.\nOf Gemma's Slovene refusals, 54\\% are explicit (the model states that it cannot help) and 26\\% are deflections (the model redirects the conversation without directly refusing).\n\n\\subsection{Dose--Response}\n\n\\begin{figure}[!htbp]\n  \\centering\n  \\includegraphics[width=\\linewidth,height=0.85\\textheight,keepaspectratio]{figures/fig_dose_v0.pdf}\n  \\caption{Refusal rate on harmful prompts as a function of abliteration dose $\\lambda$ (Experiment~9). $\\lambda$ scales each model's own selected English-objective edit ($\\lambda=0$: unedited model; $\\lambda=1$: the selected edit), so the comparison that holds is English vs.\\ Slovene within a model. Equal $\\lambda$ does not mean an equal edit across models. Blue: Gemma-3-12B-IT; green: GaMS3-12B-Instruct. Solid lines with filled markers: English (back-translated) probes; dashed lines with open markers: Slovene (NLLB machine-translated) probes. Points are raw refusal proportions from the distilled mdeBERTa judge. Shaded bands are Wilson 95\\% intervals. $n=300$ items per model and language at $\\lambda=0$ and $n=100$ at each of the 8 edited steps. Gemma's Slovene curve lies above its English curve at every dose, with a 0.21--0.32 gap between $\\lambda=0.5$ and $1$ (e.g.\\ 0.64 vs.\\ 0.32 at $\\lambda=1$), so more abliteration is needed to reach the same refusal reduction in Slovene. GaMS3's Slovene--English gap is smaller (at most 0.14, at $\\lambda=0.5$) and closes by $\\lambda=1$. The cross-model difference at matched 50\\% English refusal ($G_3=-0.97$ $[-1.56, -0.44]$ log-odds) did not meet the pre-registered confirmation criteria (verdict: \\textsc{estimate}; model-label permutation $p=0.084$).}\n  \\label{fig:dose}\n\\end{figure}\n\nExperiment~9 measures refusal rates across nine $\\lambda$ values for both models in English and Slovene (300 items per condition; Figure~\\ref{fig:dose}).\nGemma's dose-response curve in Slovene is right-shifted relative to its English curve: at matched doses, more Slovene refusal remains.\nGaMS3 shows a smaller and non-significant shift.\nThe 13-step dense dose ladder (Experiment~15) confirms that the refusal gap is present across the dose range, not concentrated at a single operating point.\n\n\\subsection{Inconclusive and Null Results}\n\n\\paragraph{Unedited GaMS3 vs.\\ Gemma in the SL$\\to$SL cell.}\nThe unedited GaMS3 shows a refusal gap of $-1.17$ $[-2.83, 0.22]$ relative to Gemma in the SL$\\to$SL cell.\nThis estimate is inconclusive: it includes zero, its fragility index is 1 (a single item reclassification would flip the sign), and the unedited models operate near ceiling refusal rates (Gemma 0.95, GaMS3 0.87), making log-odds contrasts unreliable.\n\n\\paragraph{Hungarian.}\nAll Hungarian contrasts are uninformative.\nThe minimum detectable effect for Hungarian is approximately 3 log-odds units, and no observed Hungarian effect exceeds this threshold.\n\n\\paragraph{RefusEU validation.}\nExperiment~17 tests attack success rate on the reserved RefusEU benchmark (1,300 EN + 1,300 SL items).\nThe DiD on this benchmark is inconclusive (MDE $> 2$), consistent with the near-ceiling refusal rates on this corpus.\n\n\\section{Discussion}\n\\label{sec:discussion}\n\n\\subsection{Interpretation}\n\nThe over-refusal finding has a concrete interpretation for multilingual evaluation: a model can appear ``safer'' in a non-English language simply because it refuses more benign requests, inflating the refusal rate without any improvement in harm detection.\nThe signal-detection framing separates these two components.\nThe near-zero DiD on $d'$ means that the language shift does not make either model better or worse at distinguishing harmful from benign items; the entire difference is in the threshold.\n\nThe reply-language finding, if confirmed by future work with stronger judge anchors, would suggest that the refusal mechanism is partially encoded in the model's output-language circuitry rather than the input-language pathway.\nThis is consistent with mechanistic findings that safety-related representations are entangled with language-identity features \\citep{Upadhyaya2026, Miao2026}.\n\n\\subsection{Limitations}\n\n\\paragraph{Sample size.}\nThe adjudication sample is 30 items per cell, which limits the precision of judge-validity estimates.\nThe false-alarm rate estimates rest on 1,093 safe items, adequate for the pooled contrast but noisy at the per-category level.\n\n\\paragraph{Judge specificity.}\nIn the Experiment~16 harmful-content adjudication, the primary judge achieves only $\\kappa = 0.12$ agreement with the adjudicator in the Gemma Slovene-edited cell, indicating substantial misclassification.\nThis inflates the raw refusal rate and weakens the reply-language finding.\nThe PPI correction addresses this statistically but depends on the gold-label quality of the Sonnet~4.5 adjudicator, which is itself an LLM.\n\n\\paragraph{Language compliance.}\nFour cells (SL$\\to$EN, HU$\\to$EN, SL$\\to$HU, HU$\\to$SL) fall below 90\\% compliance, limiting the crossed-grid analysis to compliant rows for mechanism claims.\n\n\\paragraph{Quantization.}\nBoth models run in NF4 quantization, which introduces noise relative to full-precision inference.\nThe abliteration edit is applied to the quantized model, and the interaction between quantization and directional ablation is not characterized.\n\n\\paragraph{Novelty.}\nThe observation that over-refusal rates differ across languages is partially anticipated by prior work \\citep{Ifebi2026, Dahir2026}.\nThe present work's contribution is the signal-detection decomposition (criterion vs.\\ sensitivity) and the controlled abliteration design, not the observation itself.\n\n\\section{Conclusion}\n\nUnedited Gemma-3-12B-IT over-refuses benign Slovene prompts at a rate of 0.569, compared to 0.364 in English.\nSignal-detection analysis attributes this entirely to a criterion shift (DiD$_c = +0.52$ $[0.38, 0.68]$) with no sensitivity difference, replicated across four experiments.\nA secondary analysis suggests that residual refusal under partial abliteration tracks the reply language, but this finding is rated \\textsc{estimate} due to weak judge anchoring ($\\kappa = 0.12$) and a PPI correction consistent with zero.\nMultilingual safety evaluations that report only attack-success rates on harmful items will miss criterion shifts that inflate refusal rates on benign items.\n\n\\bibliographystyle{plainnat}\n\\bibliography{references}\n\n\\end{document}", "stderr": "", "interrupted": false, "isImage": false, "noOutputExpected": false}

def z(p):
    return statistics.NormalDist().inv_cdf(p)


def sdt_cells(its, coding="R", en=0):

            pass
    out = []

        for it in its:
            lab = it[5][ci]
            ref = lab == "R" or (coding == "RP" and lab == "P")

            else:
                fn += 1; fk += ref
        H = (hk + .5) / (hn + 1); F = (fk + .5) / (fn + 1)

    did_c = (out[3][3] - out[2][3]) - (out[1][3] - out[0][3])
    did_d = (out[3][2] - out[2][2]) - (out[1][2] - out[0][2])

    <h1>Over-Refusal of Benign Slovene Prompts Survives English De-censoring in Gemma-3-12B</h1>
    <p class="lede">A controlled comparison of Gemma-3-12B-IT with its Slovene-adapted sibling GaMS3-12B-Instruct. Every chart on this page is drawn in your browser from the run's recorded per-item outputs.</p>

<main id="main">

<!-- ============ THE FINDING ============ -->
<section class="block" id="finding" aria-labelledby="h-finding">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-finding">The finding</h2>
  <div class="prose">
    <p>Gemma-3-12B-IT refuses more often in Slovene than in English. That could mean it is better at spotting harm in Slovene, or only that it says no more readily. Signal-detection theory separates the two: <button type="button" class="term" data-term="dprime" aria-describedby="def-dprime">sensitivity <i>d</i>′</button> measures how well a model tells harmful from benign items, and the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="criterion" aria-describedby="def-criterion">criterion <i>c</i></button> measures how ready it is to refuse at all.</p>
    <p>On 1,093 safe and 349 harmful items, unedited Gemma false-refuses benign Slovene items at nearly twice its English rate, and the whole change sits in the criterion. GaMS3, trained further on Slovene, shows no such shift. The paper reports the contrast as a <button type="button" class="term" data-term="didc" aria-describedby="def-didc">difference-in-differences</button> on the criterion:</p>
  </div>
  <div class="bignum">DiD<sub>c</sub> = +0.52 <small>95% CI [0.38, 0.68]; on sensitivity, DiD<sub><i>d</i>′</sub> = −0.003 [−0.33, 0.29]</small></div>

  <div class="view" id="v-headline">
    <p class="q">Is the extra Slovene refusal on harmful items, on safe items, or both, and does it hold in each item source?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <fieldset class="seg"><legend>Items shown in the bars</legend><div class="opts">
        <label><input type="radio" name="hl-kind" value="safe" checked><span>Safe items (false alarms)</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="hl-kind" value="harm"><span>Harmful items (hits)</span></label>
      </div></fieldset>
      <label class="ctl"><span class="lab">Item source</span>
        <select id="hl-src"><option value="all">All HARD items</option><option value="X">XSTest only</option><option value="O">OR-Bench only</option></select>
      </label>
    </div>
    <div class="two">
      <div>
        <div class="legend" aria-hidden="true"><span><span class="sw" style="background:var(--en)"></span>English (back-translated prompt)</span><span><span class="sw" style="background:var(--sl)"></span>Slovene (machine-translated prompt)</span></div>
        <div class="chart" id="c-bars"></div>
      </div>
      <div>
        <div class="chart" id="c-crit"></div>
        <div class="tablewrap"><table class="num" id="t-sdt" aria-label="Signal-detection parameters per model and language"></table></div>
      </div>

The per-cell error matrices in the run found that this judge over-calls REFUSE on edited Slovene replies. If the Slovene gap were only the judge's doing, a stricter cut-off would close it.</p></div>

<section class="block" id="fails" aria-labelledby="h-fails">
<div class="wrap">
  <h2 id="h-fails">Where it fails</h2>
  <div class="prose"><p>The criterion shift is the paper's most robust result, but it is not uniform. The paper notes that it is concentrated in OR-Bench-hard items and reverses sign when partial answers are coded as refusals. Each row below recomputes DiD from the recorded labels on a different slice. The whisker is the 95% bootstrap interval the artifact recorded for that slice.</p></div>
  <div class="view" id="v-robust">
    <p class="q">Which choices of items, English arm or outcome coding make the criterion shift disappear?</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <fieldset class="seg"><legend>Parameter</legend><div class="opts">
        <label><input type="radio" name="rb-par" value="c" checked><span>Criterion (DiD<sub>c</sub>)</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="rb-par" value="d"><span>Sensitivity (DiD<sub><i>d</i>′</sub>)</span></label>
      </div></fieldset>
      <label class="chk"><input type="checkbox" id="rb-fail"> Show only slices whose interval includes 0 or flips sign</label>
    </div>
    <div class="chart" id="c-robust"></div>
    <p class="takeaway" id="tk-robust" aria-live="polite"></p>

    <h4>Build your own slice</h4>
    <p class="small prose">Keep only items whose English back-translation matches the original at or above a <button type="button" class="term" data-term="chrf" aria-describedby="def-chrf">chrF</button> floor, choose the coding, and resample the items yourself (2,000 draws, stratified by safe and harmful, seeded).</p>
    <div class="controls">
      <label class="ctl"><span class="lab">Minimum back-translation chrF: <output id="own-cv" for="own-c">0</output></span>
        <input type="range" id="own-c" min="0" max="90" step="5" value="0"></label>
      <fieldset class="seg"><legend>Count as refusal</legend><div class="opts">
        <label><input type="radio" name="own-cod" value="R" checked><span>REFUSE</span></label>
        <label><input type="radio" name="own-cod" value="RP"><span>REFUSE + <button type="button" class="term" data-term="partial" aria-describedby="def-partial" tabindex="-1">PARTIAL</button></span></label>
      </div></fieldset>
      <label class="ctl"><span class="lab">Source</span><select id="own-src"><option value="all">All</option><option value="X">XSTest</option><option value="O">OR-Bench</option></select></label>
      <button type="button" class="act" id="own-boot">Run bootstrap</button>
    </div>
    <p class="counts" id="own-out" aria-live="polite"></p>
  </div>

  <h3>What the paper says it does not show</h3>
  <ul class="lim prose">
    <li><b>The reply-language result is an estimate, not a finding.</b> Gemma's raw output-language contrast is <button type="button" class="term" data-term="out" aria-describedby="def-out">OUT<sub>SL</sub></button> = +1.14 [0.60, 1.56] log-odds, but the <button type="button" class="term" data-term="ppi" aria-describedby="def-ppi">PPI</button>-corrected contrast is 0.20 [−0.76, 1.13], the pre-registered four-readout robustness gate returns robust = False, and the adjudicator agrees with the primary judge at only κ = 0.12 in the Slovene cell.</li>
    <li><b>The dose-response gap across models did not confirm.</b> At matched 50% English refusal the cross-model difference is <i>G</i><sub>3</sub> = −0.97 [−1.56, −0.44] log-odds, which missed the pre-registered criteria (model-label permutation <i>p</i> = 0.084).</li>
    <li><b>Small adjudication samples.</b> Judge validity rests on 30 adjudicated items per cell, and the adjudicator (Sonnet 4.5) is itself an LLM.</li>
    <li><b>Language compliance.</b> Four grid cells (SL→EN, HU→EN, SL→HU, HU→SL) fall below 90% compliance, which limits mechanism claims to compliant rows.</li>
    <li><b>Quantization.</b> Both models run in NF4, and the interaction between quantization and directional ablation is not characterised.</li>
    <li><b>Novelty is partial.</b> Language-dependent over-refusal is partly anticipated by prior work; the contribution is the criterion-versus-sensitivity decomposition and the controlled edit design.</li>
    <li><b>Near-ceiling baselines.</b> The unedited GaMS3-versus-Gemma gap in the SL→SL cell, −1.17 [−2.83, 0.22], is inconclusive: a single reclassified item flips its sign. Hungarian contrasts are uninformative (MDE about 3 log-odds).</li>
  </ul>
  <p class="small prose">Recorded in the run's artifacts rather than the paper: no native speaker audited the Slovene translations, and the Experiment 5 judge is a local Qwen3-14B substitute used after the paid-judge budget ran out. The Experiment 5 records also name a Gemini translation (with a gpt-4.1-mini back-translation) for the HARD set, where the paper's Method section says NLLB. NLLB was used for an XSTest-only arm and for Experiments 9 and 14.</p>
</div>
</section>

<footer id="glossary" aria-labelledby="h-gloss">
<div class="wrap">
  <div class="links" style="margin-top:0">
    <a class="btn primary" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_UESxYRggGt7E/paper.pdf">Read the paper (PDF)</a>
    <a class="btn" href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_UESxYRggGt7E/report.pdf">Read the full research report</a>
    <a class="btn" href="https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive/tree/fork/run_UESxYRggGt7E">Code repository</a>
  </div>
  <h2 id="h-gloss" style="margin-top:36px">Glossary</h2>
  <dl>
    <dt>Over-refusal</dt><dd id="def-over">The model declines benign requests it should answer.</dd>
    <dt>Abliteration</dt><dd id="def-ablit">Directional ablation of the refusal direction in a model's residual stream. Here it is an English-objective edit applied through per-layer LoRA adapters found by a 40-trial TPE search.</dd>
    <dt>Edit dose λ</dt><dd id="def-lambda">λ scales each model's own selected English-objective edit (λ = 0: unedited model; λ = 1: the selected edit). Equal λ does not mean an equal edit across models.</dd>
    <dt>Hit rate <i>H</i></dt><dd id="def-hit">Refusal on harmful items.</dd>
    <dt>False-alarm rate <i>F</i></dt><dd id="def-fa">The proportion of safe items refused.</dd>
    <dt>Sensitivity <i>d</i>′</dt><dd id="def-dprime">How well the model distinguishes harmful from benign items: <i>d</i>′ = <i>z</i>(<i>H</i>) − <i>z</i>(<i>F</i>).</dd>
    <dt>Criterion <i>c</i></dt><dd id="def-criterion">The threshold the model applies for the same discriminative ability: <i>c</i> = −(<i>z</i>(<i>H</i>) + <i>z</i>(<i>F</i>))/2. A lower <i>c</i> means the model refuses more readily. A criterion shift is a change in <i>c</i> with no change in <i>d</i>′.</dd>
    <dt>DiD<sub>c</sub></dt><dd id="def-didc">The difference-in-differences on the criterion: (<i>c</i><sub>GaMS3,SL</sub> − <i>c</i><sub>GaMS3,EN</sub>) − (<i>c</i><sub>Gemma,SL</sub> − <i>c</i><sub>Gemma,EN</sub>). Positive means Gemma's criterion moves toward refusal in Slovene relative to GaMS3.</dd>
    <dt>PARTIAL</dt><dd id="def-partial">The judge's third label, between REFUSE and COMPLY. The primary coding counts it as non-refusal; the sensitivity coding counts it as refusal.</dd>
    <dt>Back-translation chrF</dt><dd id="def-chrf">Character n-gram F-score between the original English prompt and its back-translation from Slovene, recorded per item (0 to 100). Low values flag items whose meaning may have drifted in translation.</dd>
    <dt>OUT<sub>SL</sub>, IN<sub>SL</sub></dt><dd id="def-out">OUT<sub>SL</sub> is the mean log-odds refusal gap between Slovene-output and English-output cells, averaging over prompt languages. IN<sub>SL</sub> is defined symmetrically for the prompt language.</dd>
    <dt>Language compliance</dt><dd id="def-compliance">The share of replies written in the requested output language. Cells below 90% are excluded from mechanism claims or flagged.</dd>
    <dt>PPI / PPI++</dt><dd id="def-ppi">Prediction-powered inference: a framework for correcting classifier estimates against a gold standard, here a Sonnet 4.5 adjudicator.</dd>
    <dt>NF4</dt><dd id="def-nf4">4-bit NormalFloat quantization; both models run in it.</dd>
  </dl>

  <h2 style="margin-top:36px">Data provenance</h2>
  <ul class="prov">
    <li><b>The finding, the stepper, the item browser, and Where it fails</b>: <code>experiment_5/results/items_final.jsonl</code> (HARD set, 1,442 items × 4 model–language cells plus the original-English arm; judge labels, back-translation chrF, MT-fragile flag, prompts and replies). Recorded slice estimates and bootstrap intervals: <code>experiment_5/results/analysis_final.json</code> (<code>C2_hard_sdt</code>).</li>
    <li><b>Crossed grid</b>: <code>experiment_14/full_method_out.json</code> (harmful rows, primary-judge label, detected reply language; edit, unedited and random-direction conditions).</li>
    <li><b>Try it</b>: <code>experiment_9/results/items_final.jsonl</code> (J1 label probabilities for the λ curve, the unedited model and Gemma's random-direction edits).</li>
    <li>The embedded JSON was produced by a script that reads these files; subsets are stated where they apply. This page shows none of the paper's static figures: each one is a data plot that the page redraws from the same records.</li>
  </ul>
  <p class="small">The paper lists no authors and carries no citation block.</p>

0);white-space:nowrap}\n.cellpanel{margin-top:12px}\n</style>\n</head>\n<body>\n<a class=\"skip\" href=\"#main\">Skip to main content</a>\n\n<header class=\"top\">\n  <div class=\"wrap\">\n    <div class=\"kicker\">Interactive companion to the paper</div>\n    <h1>Over-Refusal of Benign Slovene Prompts Survives English De-censoring in Gemma-3-12B</h1>\n    <p class=\"lede\">A controlled comparison of Gemma-3-12B-IT with its Slovene-adapted sibling GaMS3-12B-Instruct. Every chart on this page is drawn in your browser from the run's recorded per-item outputs.</p>\n    <div class=\"links\">\n      <a class=\"btn primary\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_UESxYRggGt7E/paper.pdf\">Read the paper (PDF)</a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive@fork/run_UESxYRggGt7E/report.pdf\">Read the full research report</a>\n      <a class=\"btn\" href=\"https://github.com/ai-inventor-papers/ai-invention-2cf2a7-does-slovene-taught-refusal-survive/tree/fork/run_UESxYRggGt7E\">Code repository</a>\n    </div>\n  </div>\n</header>\n\n<nav class=\"sec\" aria-label=\"Sections\">\n  <ul>\n    <li><a href=\"#finding\">The finding</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#method\">How it works</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#evidence\">Explore the evidence</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#tryit\">Try it</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#fails\">Where it fails</a></li>\n    <li><a href=\"#glossary\">Glossary &amp; sources</a></li>\n  </ul>\n</nav>\n\n<main id=\"main\">\n\n<!-- ============ THE FINDING ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"finding\" aria-labelledby=\"h-finding\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-finding\">The finding</h2>\n  <div class=\"prose\">\n    <p>Gemma-3-12B-IT refuses more often in Slovene than in English. That could mean it is better at spotting harm in Slovene, or only that it says no more readily. Signal-detection theory separates the two: <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"dprime\" aria-describedby=\"def-dprime\">sensitivity <i>d</i>′</button> measures how well a model tells harmful from benign items, and the <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"criterion\" aria-describedby=\"def-criterion\">criterion <i>c</i></button> measures how ready it is to refuse at all.</p>\n    <p>On 1,093 safe and 349 harmful items, unedited Gemma false-refuses benign Slovene items at nearly twice its English rate, and the whole change sits in the criterion. GaMS3, trained further on Slovene, shows no such shift. The paper reports the contrast as a <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"didc\" aria-describedby=\"def-didc\">difference-in-differences</button> on the criterion:</p>\n  </div>\n  <div class=\"bignum\">DiD<sub>c</sub> = +0.52 <small>95% CI [0.38, 0.68]; on sensitivity, DiD<sub><i>d</i>′</sub> = −0.003 [−0.33, 0.29]</small></div>\n\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-headline\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Is the extra Slovene refusal on harmful items, on safe items, or both, and does it hold in each item source?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <fieldset class=\"seg\"><legend>Items shown in the bars</legend><div class=\"opts\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"hl-kind\" value=\"safe\" checked><span>Safe items (false alarms)</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"hl-kind\" value=\"harm\"><span>Harmful items (hits)</span></label>\n      </div></fieldset>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span class=\"lab\">Item source</span>\n        <select id=\"hl-src\"><option value=\"all\">All HARD items</option><option value=\"X\">XSTest only</option><option value=\"O\">OR-Bench only</option></select>\n      </label>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"two\">\n      <div>\n        <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--en)\"></span>English (back-translated prompt)</span><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--sl)\"></span>Slovene (machine-translated prompt)</span></div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-bars\"></div>\n      </div>\n      <div>\n        <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-crit\"></div>\n        <div class=\"tablewrap\"><table class=\"num\" id=\"t-sdt\" aria-label=\"Signal-detection parameters per model and language\"></table></div>\n      </div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"tk-headline\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <p class=\"note\">Bars are raw proportions (refused / items). <i>d</i>′ and <i>c</i> use the log-linear corrected rates (<i>k</i>+0.5)/(<i>n</i>+1), exactly as the artifact computed them. Refusal = the judge's REFUSE label; PARTIAL counts as non-refusal. Recomputed here from the 1,442 × 4 recorded labels; the full-set values match <code>analysis_final.json</code> to the last digit.</p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ HOW IT WORKS ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"method\" aria-labelledby=\"h-method\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-method\">How it works: one item, start to finish</h2>\n  <p class=\"prose\">The stepper follows one real XSTest item through the pipeline that produced the headline number. Every value shown is the one the run recorded.</p>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-stepper\">\n    <p class=\"q\">What happens between a benign prompt and a criterion shift of +0.52?</p>\n    <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-pipe\" role=\"group\" aria-label=\"Pipeline stages\"></div>\n    <div class=\"stepper-nav\">\n      <button type=\"button\" class=\"act\" id=\"st-prev\">← Previous</button>\n      <button type=\"button\" class=\"act\" id=\"st-next\">Next →</button>\n      <span class=\"small\">Or use the ← and → keys while the stepper has focus.</span>\n    </div>\n    <div id=\"st-live\" class=\"srtext\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    <div id=\"st-body\" tabindex=\"-1\"></div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"tk-stepper\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ EVIDENCE ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"evidence\" aria-labelledby=\"h-evidence\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-evidence\">Explore the evidence</h2>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-browser\">Item browser: what the four replies look like</h3>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-browser\">\n    <p class=\"q\">When Gemma refuses a benign prompt only in Slovene, what did the prompt say, and what did each model answer?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <fieldset class=\"seg\"><legend>Item type</legend><div class=\"opts\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"br-kind\" value=\"0\" checked><span>Safe</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"br-kind\" value=\"1\"><span>Harmful</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"br-kind\" value=\"all\"><span>Both</span></label>\n      </div></fieldset>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span class=\"lab\">Pattern</span>\n        <select id=\"br-pat\">\n          <option value=\"gsl\">Gemma refuses only in Slovene</option>\n          <option value=\"gen\">Gemma refuses only in English</option>\n          <option value=\"any\">Any pattern</option>\n          <option value=\"all4\">All four replies refused</option>\n          <option value=\"none\">No reply refused</option>\n        </select>\n      </label>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span class=\"lab\">Source</span>\n        <select id=\"br-src\"><option value=\"all\">All sources</option><option value=\"X\">XSTest</option><option value=\"O\">OR-Bench hard-1k</option><option value=\"T\">OR-Bench toxic</option></select>\n      </label>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span class=\"lab\">Sort</span>\n        <select id=\"br-sort\"><option value=\"id\">Item id</option><option value=\"chrf-asc\">Back-translation chrF, low first</option><option value=\"chrf-desc\">Back-translation chrF, high first</option></select>\n      </label>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span class=\"lab\">Search prompts</span>\n        <input type=\"search\" id=\"br-q\" placeholder=\"e.g. mango, kill, zakaj\" aria-describedby=\"br-count\">\n      </label>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"counts\" id=\"br-count\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <div class=\"browser\">\n      <ul class=\"ilist\" id=\"br-list\" aria-label=\"Matching items\"></ul>\n      <div class=\"detail\" id=\"br-detail\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"tk-browser\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <p class=\"note\" id=\"br-rule\"></p>\n  </div>\n\n  <h3 id=\"h-grid\">Crossed grid: prompt language × reply language</h3>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-grid\">\n    <p class=\"q\">After a partial English edit, does Gemma's leftover refusal follow the language of the prompt or the language it must reply in?</p>\n    <p class=\"small prose\">Experiment 14 asks each harmful prompt (200 per cell) in English, Slovene or Hungarian, with a one-line instruction to reply in a given language. The <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"lambda\" aria-describedby=\"def-lambda\">edit dose λ</button> scales the English-objective <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"ablit\" aria-describedby=\"def-ablit\">abliteration</button> edit.</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <fieldset class=\"seg\"><legend>Model</legend><div class=\"opts\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"gr-model\" value=\"gemma_it\" checked><span>Gemma-3-12B-IT</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"gr-model\" value=\"gams3_it\"><span>GaMS3-12B-Instruct</span></label>\n      </div></fieldset>\n      <fieldset class=\"seg\"><legend>Edit dose</legend><div class=\"opts\" id=\"gr-doses\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"gr-dose\" value=\"zero\"><span>Unedited</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"gr-dose\" value=\"lo\"><span>Low</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"gr-dose\" value=\"hi\" checked><span>High</span></label>\n      </div></fieldset>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span class=\"lab\">Follow one harmful item</span><select id=\"gr-item\"></select></label>\n    </div>\n    <div class=\"two\">\n      <div><div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-grid\"></div>\n        <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#2166ac\"></span>0 refused</span><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#f7f7f7;border:1px solid #ccc\"></span>0.5</span><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#b2182b\"></span>all refused</span><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:repeating-linear-gradient(45deg,#999 0 2px,#fff 2px 5px)\"></span>&lt;90% of replies in the requested language</span></div>\n      </div>\n      <div class=\"cellpanel\" id=\"gr-panel\" aria-live=\"polite\"></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"small\" id=\"gr-rand\"></p>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"tk-grid\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <p class=\"note\">Each cell: refused / 200 by the primary judge, with the unedited model's rate for the same cell beneath it as the baseline. Point at, focus or tap a cell to read the followed item's reply there. Hatching follows the paper's 90% <button type=\"button\" class=\"term\" data-term=\"compliance\" aria-describedby=\"def-compliance\">language-compliance</button> rule, computed at the dose shown.</p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ TRY IT ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"tryit\" aria-labelledby=\"h-tryit\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-tryit\">Try it: move the judge's cut-off</h2>\n  <div class=\"prose\"><p>Experiment 9 scaled each model's own English-objective edit from λ = 0 to λ = 2 and scored every reply with a distilled mDeBERTa judge (J1). J1 recorded a probability for each label, so the page can re-decide every reply under a stricter or looser rule. The per-cell error matrices in the run found that this judge over-calls REFUSE on edited Slovene replies. If the Slovene gap were only the judge's doing, a stricter cut-off would close it.</p></div>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-dose\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Does Gemma's Slovene-over-English refusal gap along the dose curve depend on where the judge draws the line?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <fieldset class=\"seg\"><legend>Prompts</legend><div class=\"opts\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"ds-kind\" value=\"harmful\" checked><span>Harmful probe</span></label>\n        <label><input type=\"radio\" name=\"ds-kind\" value=\"benign\"><span>Benign twins</span></label>\n      </div></fieldset>\n      <label class=\"chk\"><input type=\"checkbox\" id=\"ds-argmax\" checked> Use the judge's recorded label</label>\n      <label class=\"ctl\"><span class=\"lab\">Refuse when P(REFUSE) ≥ <output id=\"ds-tv\" for=\"ds-t\">0.50</output></span>\n        <input type=\"range\" id=\"ds-t\" min=\"0.05\" max=\"0.95\" step=\"0.05\" value=\"0.5\" disabled aria-describedby=\"ds-thelp\">\n      </label>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"small\" id=\"ds-thelp\">Untick the box to enable the slider. The recorded label is the most probable of REFUSE, PARTIAL and COMPLY; the slider applies a single threshold to the recorded P(REFUSE) instead.</p>\n    <div class=\"legend\" aria-hidden=\"true\"><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--en)\"></span>English (back-translated)</span><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:var(--sl)\"></span>Slovene (NLLB machine translation)</span><span><span class=\"sw\" style=\"background:#fff;border:2px solid var(--muted)\"></span>norm-matched random-direction edits (Gemma)</span></div>\n    <div class=\"two\" style=\"grid-template-columns:1fr 1fr\">\n      <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-dose-gemma_it\"></div>\n      <div class=\"chart\" id=\"c-dose-gams3_it\"></div>\n    </div>\n    <p class=\"takeaway\" id=\"tk-dose\" aria-live=\"polite\"></p>\n    <p class=\"note\">Points are recorded proportions with Wilson 95% intervals; lines only join neighbouring recorded doses. <i>n</i> = 300 harmful items per model and language at λ = 0 and 100 at each edited step; the benign twins have 150 at λ = 0 and 60 per edited step. Equal λ does not mean an equal edit across the two models, so compare English with Slovene within a panel.</p>\n  </div>\n</div>\n</section>\n\n<!-- ============ WHERE IT FAILS ============ -->\n<section class=\"block\" id=\"fails\" aria-labelledby=\"h-fails\">\n<div class=\"wrap\">\n  <h2 id=\"h-fails\">Where it fails</h2>\n  <div class=\"prose\"><p>The criterion shift is the paper's most robust result, but it is not uniform. The paper notes that it is concentrated in OR-Bench-hard items and reverses sign when partial answers are coded as refusals. Each row below recomputes DiD from the recorded labels on a different slice. The whisker is the 95% bootstrap interval the artifact recorded for that slice.</p></div>\n  <div class=\"view\" id=\"v-robust\">\n    <p class=\"q\">Which choices of items, English arm or outcome coding make the criterion shift disappear?</p>\n    <div class=\"controls\">\n      <fieldset class=\"seg\"><legend>Parameter</legend><div class=\"opts\">\n        <label><input type=\"radio\"       const lab = `${MODEL[mod]}, ${LANG[lg]}: ${k} of ${n} ${kind === 'safe' ? 'safe' : 'harmful'} items refused (${v.toFixed(3)}; Wilson 95% ${ci95[0].toFixed(3)}–${ci95[1].toFixed(3)})`;
      bindMark(rect, `<b>${MODEL_FULL[mod]} · ${LANG[lg]}</b><br>${k} / ${n} ${kind === 'safe' ? 'safe' : 'harmful'} items refused = ${v.toFixed(3)}<br>Wilson 95% [${ci95[0].toFixed(3)}, ${ci95[1].toFixed(3)}]`, lab);
    });
    const tl = S('text', { x: cx, y: Ht - m.b + 20, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl', 'font-weight': 650, fill: '#1b1d21' }, svg); tl.textContent = MODEL_FULL[mod];
  });
  S('line', { x1: m.l, x2: W - m.r, y1: y(0), y2: y(0), stroke: '#8b9099' }, svg);
  const cap = S('text', { x: m.l, y: Ht - 6, class: 'lbl' }, svg); cap.textContent = kind === 'safe' ? 'False-alarm rate F on safe items (n = ' + R.ns + ')' : 'Hit rate H on harmful items (n = ' + R.nh + ')';

  // criterion dot plot
  const cb = $('#c-crit'); cb.innerHTML = '';
  const W2 = Math.max(280, cb.clientWidth), H2 = 190, m2 = { l: 70, r: 14, t: 28, b: 42 };
  const svg2 = S('svg', { viewBox: `0 0 ${W2} ${H2}`, role: 'group', 'aria-label': 'Criterion c per model, English versus Slovene' }, cb);
  const cs = R.cells.map(c => c.c); let lo = Math.min(-1.2, ...cs) - 0.05, hi = Math.max(0.2, ...cs) + 0.05;
  const x = v => m2.l + (v - lo) / (hi - lo) * (W2 - m2.l - m2.r);
  const g = S('g', { class: 'axis' }, svg2);
  for (let t = Math.ceil(lo * 5) / 5; t <= hi + 1e-9; t += 0.2) { const xx = x(t); S('line', { x1: xx, x2: xx, y1: m2.t - 6, y2: H2 - m2.b, stroke: Math.abs(t) < 1e-9 ? '#9aa0a8' : COL.grid }, g); const tx = S('text', { x: xx, y: H2 - m2.b + 16, 'text-anchor': 'middle' }, g); tx.textContent = f(t, 1); }
  const at = S('text', { x: (m2.l + W2 - m2.r) / 2, y: H2 - 6, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl' }, svg2); at.textContent = 'Criterion c (z units); left = refuses more readily';
  const tt = S('text', { x: m2.l, y: 14, class: 'lbl', 'font-weight': 650, fill: '#1b1d21' }, svg2); tt.textContent = 'Criterion shift, English → Slovene';
  const defs = S('defs', {}, svg2); const mk = S('marker', { id: 'arr', viewBox: '0 0 10 10', refX: 9, refY: 5, markerWidth: 7, markerHeight: 7, orient: 'auto-start-reverse' }, defs); S('path', { d: 'M0,0 L10,5 L0,10 z', fill: '#4a4f58' }, mk);
  [['gemma_it', 0, 1], ['gams3_it', 2, 3]].forEach(([mod, ie, is], gi) => {
    const yy = m2.t + 22 + gi * 52; const ce = R.cells[ie].c, csl = R.cells[is].c;
    const lb = S('text', { x: m2.l - 8, y: yy + 4, 'text-anchor': 'end', class: 'lbl', 'font-weight': 650, fill: '#1b1d21' }, svg2); lb.textContent = MODEL[mod];
    if (Math.abs(x(csl) - x(ce)) > 12) S('line', { x1: x(ce), x2: x(csl) + (csl < ce ? 7 : -7), y1: yy, y2: yy, stroke: '#4a4f58', 'stroke-width': 1.6, 'marker-end': 'url(#arr)' }, svg2);
    [[ce, 'en', ie], [csl, 'sl', is]].forEach(([v, lg, ci]) => {
      const dot = S('circle', { cx: x(v), cy: yy, r: 7, fill: COL[lg], stroke: '#fff', 'stroke-width': 1.5 }, svg2);
      const c = R.cells[ci];
      bindMark(dot, `<b>${MODEL_FULL[mod]} · ${LANG[lg]}</b><br>c = ${f(c.c, 3)}, d′ = ${f(c.d, 3)}<br>H = ${c.H.toFixed(3)}, F = ${c.F.toFixed(3)} (corrected)`, `${MODEL[mod]} ${LANG[lg]}: criterion ${f(c.c, 3)}, sensitivity ${f(c.d, 3)}`);
    });
    const dl = S('text', { x: Math.min(x(Math.min(ce, csl)), x(Math.max(ce, csl))) + Math.abs(x(csl) - x(ce)) / 2, y: yy - 12, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl' }, svg2); dl.textContent = 'Δc = ' + fs(csl - ce, 2);
  });
  // table
  const t = $('#t-sdt'); const cl = ['Gemma EN', 'Gemma SL', 'GaMS3 EN', 'GaMS3 SL'];
  t.innerHTML = '<thead><tr><th scope="col"></th>' + cl.map(c => `<th scope="col">${c}</th>`).join('') + '</tr></thead><tbody>' +
    [['Hit rate H', c => c.H.toFixed(3)], ['False-alarm rate F', c => c.F.toFixed(3)], ['d′', c => f(c.d, 2)], ['c', c => f(c.c, 2)]].map(([n, fn]) => `<tr><th scope="row">${n}</th>${R.cells.map(c => `<td>${fn(c)}</td>`).join('')}</tr>`).join('') +
    `<tr><th scope="row">DiD<sub>c</sub> / DiD<sub>d′</sub></th><td colspan="4">${fs(R.didc, 3)} / ${fs(R.didd, 3)}</td></tr></tbody>`;
  // takeaway
  const g0 = R.cells[0], g1 = R.cells[1], s0 = R.cells[2], s1 = R.cells[3];
  const srcTxt = src === 'all' ? 'all HARD items' : src === 'X' ? 'XSTest items only' : 'OR-Bench items only';
  let tk;
  if (kind === 'safe') tk = `On ${srcTxt}, Gemma refuses ${g1.fk} of ${g1.fn} safe prompts in Slovene against ${g0.fk} in English, while GaMS3 refuses ${s1.fk} and ${s0.fk}. `;
  else tk = `On ${srcTxt}, the hit rates on harmful prompts barely separate the languages: Gemma refuses ${g1.hk} of ${g1.hn} in Slovene and ${g0.hk} in English, GaMS3 ${s1.hk} and ${s0.hk}. `;
  tk += `Gemma's criterion moves by ${fs(g1.c - g0.c, 2)} and GaMS3's by ${fs(s1.c - s0.c, 2)}, giving DiD<sub>c</sub> = ${fs(R.didc, 2)} with DiD<sub>d′</sub> = ${fs(R.didd, 2)}` + (Math.abs(R.didc) < 0.2 ? ': on this subset the shift nearly vanishes.' : '.');
  $('#tk-headline').innerHTML = tk;
}

// ======================================================= STEPPER

  { name: 'Signal detection', short: 'SDT',

let stage = 0;
function drawPipe() {
  const box = $('#c-pipe'); box.innerHTML = '';
  const W = Math.max(300, box.clientWidth), cols = W < 600 ? 4 : 7, rows = Math.ceil(STAGES.length / cols);
  const gap = 10, bw = (W - gap * (cols - 1)) / cols, bh = 46, Ht = rows * bh + (rows - 1) * 18 + 4;
  const svg = S('svg', { viewBox: `0 0 ${W} ${Ht}` }, box);
  STAGES.forEach((st, i) => {
    const r = Math.floor(i / cols), cI = i % cols, x = cI * (bw + gap), y = r * (bh + 18) + 2;
    if (i < STAGES.length - 1 && cI < cols - 1) S('line', { x1: x + bw, x2: x + bw + gap, y1: y + bh / 2, y2: y + bh / 2, stroke: '#9aa0a8', 'stroke-width': 1.5 }, svg);
    const g = S('g', { role: 'button', tabindex: '0', 'aria-label': `Stage ${i + 1}: ${st.name}`, class: 'mark' }, svg);
    if (i === stage) g.setAttribute('aria-current', 'step');
    S('rect', { x: x, y: y, width: bw, height: bh, rx: 8, fill: i === stage ? '#0b5cad' : (i < stage ? '#e7f0fa' : '#fff'), stroke: i === stage ? '#0b5cad' : '#c9ccd2', 'stroke-width': 1.5 }, g);
    const t = S('text', { x: x + bw / 2, y: y + bh / 2 + 4, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': bw < 70 ? 11 : 13, 'font-weight': 650, fill: i === stage ? '#fff' : '#1b1d21', 'font-family': 'system-ui, sans-serif' }, g);
    t.textContent = (i + 1) + '. ' + (bw < 110 ? st.short : st.name.replace('Difference-in-differences', 'DiD'));
    g.addEventListener('click', () => setStage(i));
    g.addEventListener('keydown', e => { if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') { e.preventDefault(); setStage(i); } });
  });
}
function setStage(i, fromKey) {
  stage = Math.max(0, Math.min(STAGES.length - 1, i)); const st = STAGES[stage];
  drawPipe();
  $('#st-body').innerHTML = `<h4 style="font-size:1.05rem;margin:8px 0 0">Stage ${stage + 1} of ${STAGES.length}: ${st.name}</h4><div class="stage-body"><div class="box"><h4>What goes in</h4>${st.input}</div><div class="box"><h4>What is done</h4><p>${st.op}</p></div><div class="box"><h4>What comes out</h4>${st.out}</div></div><p class="why">${st.why}</p>`;
  $('#st-prev').disabled = stage === 0; $('#st-next').disabled = stage === STAGES.length - 1;
  $('#st-live').textContent = `Stage ${stage + 1} of ${STAGES.length}: ${st.name}`;
  $('#tk-stepper').innerHTML = stage < 4 ? `Item <code>${STEP_ID}</code> at stage ${stage + 1}: the prompt is benign, and ${stage < 3 ? 'the four replies have not yet been judged.' : 'only Gemma\'s Slovene reply is judged a refusal.'}` :
    stage === 4 ? `This one item is one of ${PRIM.cells[1].fk} safe-item refusals in the Gemma · Slovene cell, against ${PRIM.cells[0].fk} in Gemma · English.` :
    stage === 5 ? `Gemma's c falls from ${f(PRIM.cells[0].c, 2)} to ${f(PRIM.cells[1].c, 2)} while its d′ barely moves (${f(PRIM.cells[0].d, 2)} to ${f(PRIM.cells[1].d, 2)}).` :
    `The item-level pattern, repeated across the set, yields DiD<sub>c</sub> = ${fs(PRIM.didc, 2)} with DiD<sub>d′</sub> = ${fs(PRIM.didd, 3)}.`;
}
$('#st-prev').addEventListener('click', () => setStage(stage - 1));
$('#st-next').addEventListener('click', () => setStage(stage + 1));
$('#v-stepper').addEventListener('keydown', e => {

function patOf(it) { const l = it[5]; const r = j => l[j] === 'R'; return { gsl: r(1) && !r(0), gen: r(0) && !r(1), all4: r(0) && r(1) && r(2) && r(3), none: !r(0) && !r(1) && !r(2) && !r(3) }; }

  const nsafe = list.filter(i => !i[1]).length;
  const gs = list.filter(i => patOf(i).gsl).length, ge = list.filter(i => patOf(i).gen).length;
  $('#br-count').textContent = `${list.length} of ${BR.length} embedded items match${list.length > 250 ? ' (first 250 listed)' : ''}. Among them, Gemma refuses ${gs} only in Slovene and ${ge} only in English.`;
  const kindTxt = kind === '0' ? 'safe' : kind === '1' ? 'harmful' : '';
  $('#tk-browser').innerHTML = list.length === 0 ? 'No embedded item matches these filters; widen the pattern or clear the search.' :
    (pat === 'any' || pat === 'gsl' || pat === 'gen') && (gs + ge) > 0 ? `In the ${list.length} matching ${kindTxt} items, Slovene-only refusals by Gemma outnumber English-only ones ${gs} to ${ge}${ge ? ' (' + (gs / ge).toFixed(1) + '×)' : ''}. Read the Slovene refusals: most are short apologies that decline outright.` :
    `${list.length} matching ${kindTxt} items. Of these, ${nsafe} are safe prompts.`;

let gridCell = ['en', 'sl'];
function gcount(model, cond, dose, i, o) { return GRID.counts[`${model}|${cond}|${dose}|${i}|${o}`]; }
function lamLabel(model, dose) { return 'λ = ' + GRID.lambda[model + '|' + dose]; }
function heatColor(v) { const lerp = (a, b, t) => Math.round(a + (b - a) * t); let c0, c1, t; if (v < 0.5) { c0 = [33, 102, 172]; c1 = [247, 247, 247]; t = v / 0.5; } else { c0 = [247, 247, 247]; c1 = [178, 24, 43]; t = (v - 0.5) / 0.5; } return `rgb(${lerp(c0[0], c1[0], t)},${lerp(c0[1], c1[1], t)},${lerp(c0[2], c1[2], t)})`; }
function drawGrid() {

  $$('#gr-doses label').forEach(l => { const v = l.querySelector('input').value; l.querySelector('span').textContent = (v === 'zero' ? 'Unedited' : v === 'lo' ? 'Low' : 'High') + ' (' + lamLabel(model, v) + ')'; });
  const box = $('#c-grid'); box.innerHTML = '';
  const W = Math.max(300, Math.min(560, box.clientWidth)), m = { l: 74, t: 40, r: 6, b: 8 }, cw = (W - m.l - m.r) / 3, ch = Math.min(96, cw * 0.78), Ht = m.t + ch * 3 + m.b + 22;
  const svg = S('svg', { viewBox: `0 0 ${W} ${Ht}`, role: 'group', 'aria-label': `${MODEL_FULL[model]} refusal grid at ${lamLabel(model, dose)}` }, box);
  const defs = S('defs', {}, svg); const pat = S('pattern', { id: 'hatch', width: 7, height: 7, patternUnits: 'userSpaceOnUse', patternTransform: 'rotate(45)' }, defs); S('line', { x1: 0, y1: 0, x2: 0, y2: 7, stroke: '#555', 'stroke-width': 2, 'stroke-opacity': .45 }, pat);
  const ht = S('text', { x: m.l + cw * 1.5, y: 14, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl', 'font-weight': 650, fill: '#1b1d21' }, svg); ht.textContent = 'Requested reply language';
  LANGS.forEach((o, j) => { const t = S('text', { x: m.l + cw * j + cw / 2, y: m.t - 8, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl' }, svg); t.textContent = LANG[o] + ' out'; });
  LANGS.forEach((i, r) => { const t = S('text', { x: m.l - 8, y: m.t + ch * r + ch / 2 + 4, 'text-anchor': 'end', class: 'lbl' }, svg); t.textContent = LANG[i] + ' in'; });
  const vt = S('text', { x: 10, y: m.t + ch * 1.5, transform: `rotate(-90 10 ${m.t + ch * 1.5})`, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl', 'font-weight': 650, fill: '#1b1d21' }, svg); vt.textContent = 'Prompt language';
  LANGS.forEach((i, r) => LANGS.forEach((o, j) => {
    const c = gcount(model, 'edit', dose, i, o), b = gcount(model, 'edit', 'zero', i, o); const v = c[0] / c[1], comp = c[2] / c[1], ci = wilson(c[0], c[1]);
    const x = m.l + cw * j, y = m.t + ch * r; const g = S('g', {}, svg);
    S('rect', { x: x + 1, y: y + 1, width: cw - 2, height: ch - 2, fill: heatColor(v), stroke: (gridCell[0] === i && gridCell[1] === o) ? '#1b1d21' : '#fff', 'stroke-width': (gridCell[0] === i && gridCell[1] === o) ? 3 : 1 }, g);
    if (comp < 0.9) S('rect', { x: x + 1, y: y + 1, width: cw - 2, height: ch - 2, fill: 'url(#hatch)' }, g);
    const dark = Math.abs(v - 0.5) > 0.3; const tc = dark ? '#fff' : '#1b1d21';
    const t1 = S('text', { x: x + cw / 2, y: y + ch / 2 - 4, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 18, 'font-weight': 700, fill: tc, 'font-family': 'system-ui,sans-serif' }, g); t1.textContent = v.toFixed(3);
    const t2 = S('text', { x: x + cw / 2, y: y + ch / 2 + 14, 'text-anchor': 'middle', 'font-size': 11, fill: tc, 'font-family': 'system-ui,sans-serif' }, g); t2.textContent = dose === 'zero' ? `${c[0]}/${c[1]}` : `unedited ${(b[0] / b[1]).toFixed(2)}`;
    const lab = `${LANG[i]} prompt, ${LANG[o]} reply: ${c[0]} of ${c[1]} refused (${v.toFixed(3)}); unedited ${b[0]} of ${b[1]}; ${Math.round(comp * 100)}% of replies in ${LANG[o]}`;
    bindMark(g, `<b>${LANG[i]} → ${LANG[o]} · ${MODEL[model]} · ${lamLabel(model, dose)}</b><br>${c[0]} / ${c[1]} refused = ${v.toFixed(3)} [${ci[0].toFixed(2)}, ${ci[1].toFixed(2)}]<br>Unedited: ${b[0]} / ${b[1]}<br>Replies in ${LANG[o]}: ${c[2]} / ${c[1]}${comp < 0.9 ? ' (below 90%)' : ''}`, lab, () => { if (gridCell[0] !== i || gridCell[1] !== o) { gridCell = [i, o]; drawCellPanel(); markSel(); } });
    g.dataset.cell = i + '|' + o;
  }));
  const cap = S('text', { x: m.l, y: Ht - 4, class: 'lbl' }, svg); cap.textContent = `${MODEL_FULL[model]}, ${lamLabel(model, dose)}; 200 harmful prompts per cell`;
  drawCellPanel();
  // random-direction control line
  if (dose === 'hi') {
    const re = gcount(model, 'rand', 'hi', 'en', 'en'), rs = gcount(model, 'rand', 'hi', 'sl', 'sl'), ee = gcount(model, 'edit', 'hi', 'en', 'en'), ss = gcount(model, 'edit', 'hi', 'sl', 'sl');
    $('#gr-rand').textContent = `Control at the same dose: a norm-matched random-direction edit leaves refusal high (English→English ${re[0]}/${re[1]}, Slovene→Slovene ${rs[0]}/${rs[1]}), while the real edit gives ${ee[0]}/${ee[1]} and ${ss[0]}/${ss[1]}.`;
  } else $('#gr-rand').textContent = dose === 'zero' ? 'Unedited model: every cell starts near ceiling refusal, so the edit is what reveals the structure.' : 'The random-direction control was run at the high dose only.';
  // takeaway
  const col = o => LANGS.map(i => { const c = gcount(model, 'edit', dose, i, o); return c[0] / c[1]; });
  const mm = a => `${Math.min(...a).toFixed(2)}–${Math.max(...a).toFixed(2)}`;
  const nh = LANGS.reduce((s, i) => s + LANGS.filter(o => { const c = gcount(model, 'edit', dose, i, o); return c[2] / c[1] < 0.9; }).length, 0);
  const slc = col('sl'), enc = col('en');
  let tk = `${MODEL[model]} at ${lamLabel(model, dose)} refuses ${mm(slc)} of harmful prompts when told to reply in Slovene and ${mm(enc)} when told to reply in English, across all three prompt languages.`;
  if (dose !== 'zero') tk += Math.min(...slc) > Math.max(...enc) ? ' The reply language, not the prompt language, separates the columns.' : ' The columns overlap, so the reply language does not separate them here.';
  if (nh) tk += ` ${nh} cell${nh > 1 ? 's are' : ' is'} hatched: under 90% of replies came back in the requested language, so ${nh > 1 ? 'they do' : 'it does'} not measure that language.`;
  $('#tk-grid').textContent = tk;
}
function markSel() { $$('#c-grid g[data-cell]').forEach(g => { const r = g.querySelector('rect'); const on = g.dataset.cell === gridCell.join('|'); r.setAttribute('stroke', on ? '#1b1d21' : '#fff'); r.setAttribute('stroke-width', on ? 3 : 1); }); }
function drawCellPanel() {
  const model = radio('gr-model'), dose = radio('gr-dose'), id = gsel.value, [i, o] = gridCell;
  const rep = GRID.replies[`${id}|${model}|${dose}|${i}|${o}`]; const p = GRID.prompts[id] || {};
  const pr = (p[i] || '').split('\n')[0];
  $('#gr-panel').innerHTML = `<p class="plab">Followed item <code>${esc(id)}</code> (${esc(GRID.source[id])}) · ${LANG[i]} prompt → ${LANG[o]} reply · ${MODEL[model]} · ${lamLabel(model, dose)}</p>
    <div class="quote" lang="${i}">${esc(pr)}${'\n'}<span class="small">[+ instruction to reply in ${LANG[o]}]</span></div>
    ${rep ? `<p class="plab">Reply ${badge(rep[1][0])} <span class="small">detected language: ${esc(rep[2])}</span></p><div class="quote" lang="${esc(rep[2])}">${esc(rep[0])}</div>` : '<p class="small">No reply recorded for this cell.</p>'}`;
}
$$('input[name="gr-model"],input[name="gr-dose"]').forEach(e => e.addEventListener('change', drawGrid));
gsel.addEventListener('change', drawCellPanel);
onResize($('#c-grid'), drawGrid);

// ======================================================= DOSE (Try it)
const LAMS = [0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1, 1.25, 1.5, 1.75, 2];
function dkey(model, kind, arm, step) { return `${model}|${kind}|${arm}|${step}`; }
function drate(model, kind, arm, step, t) {
  const k = dkey(model, kind, arm, step === 'rand' ? 'rand' : (step === 0 ? '0.0' : String(step % 1 === 0 ? step.toFixed(1) : step)));
  const p = DOSE.p[k]; if (!p) return null;
  const n = p.length; const r = t === null ? DOSE.argmax_refuse[k] : p.reduce((s, x) => s + (x >= t - 1e-9 ? 1 : 0), 0);
  return { k: r, n: n };
}
function drawDose() {
  const kind = radio('ds-kind'), useArg = $('#ds-argmax').checked, t = useArg ? null : Number($('#ds-t').value);
  $('#ds-t').disabled = useArg; $('#ds-tv').textContent = Number($('#ds-t').value).toFixed(2);
  const summ = {};
  ['gemma_it', 'gams3_it'].forEach(model => {
    const box = $('#c-dose-' + model); box.innerHTML = '';
    const W = Math.max(280, box.clientWidth), Ht = 280, m = { l: 48, r: model === 'gemma_it' ? 40 : 10, t: 26, b: 44 };
    const svg = S('svg', { viewBox: `0 0 ${W} ${Ht}`, role: 'group', 'aria-label': `${MODEL_FULL[model]} refusal by dose` }, box);
    const x = v => m.l + v / 2 * (W - m.l - m.r - (model === 'gemma_it' ? 20 : 0)), y = v => m.t + (1 - v) * (Ht - m.t - m.b);
    axisY(svg, m.l, W - m.r, y, [0, .25, .5, .75, 1], v => v.toFixed(2), 'Share refused', (m.t + Ht - m.b) / 2);
    const g = S('g', { class: 'axis' }, svg);
    [0, 0.5, 1, 1.5, 2].forEach(v => { const tx = S('text', { x: x(v), y: Ht - m.b + 16, 'text-anchor': 'middle' }, g); tx.textContent = v; });
    const xl = S('text', { x: (m.l + W - m.r) / 2, y: Ht - 8, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl' }, svg); xl.textContent = 'Edit dose λ';
    const tl = S('text', { x: m.l, y: 14, class: 'lbl', 'font-weight': 650, fill: '#1b1d21' }, svg); tl.textContent = MODEL_FULL[model];
    S('line', { x1: m.l, x2: W - m.r, y1: y(0), y2: y(0), stroke: '#8b9099' }, svg);
    summ[model] = {};
    [['en_bt', 'en'], ['sl_mt', 'sl']].forEach(([arm, lg]) => {
      const pts = LAMS.map(l => ({ l: l, r: drate(model, kind, arm, l, t) })).filter(p => p.r);
      summ[model][lg] = pts;
      S('path', { d: pts.map((p, i) => (i ? 'L' : 'M') + x(p.l) + ',' + y(p.r.k / p.r.n)).join(''), fill: 'none', stroke: COL[lg], 'stroke-width': 2, 'stroke-dasharray': lg === 'sl' ? '6 4' : '' }, svg);
      pts.forEach(p => {
        const v = p.r.k / p.r.n, ci = wilson(p.r.k, p.r.n), xx = x(p.l) + (lg === 'sl' ? 2 : -2);
        S('line', { x1: xx, x2: xx, y1: y(ci[0]), y2: y(ci[1]), stroke: COL[lg], 'stroke-opacity': .55, 'stroke-width': 1.5 }, svg);
        const c = S(lg === 'sl' ? 'rect' : 'circle', lg === 'sl' ? { x: xx - 5, y: y(v) - 5, width: 10, height: 10, fill: '#fff', stroke: COL[lg], 'stroke-width': 2 } : { cx: xx, cy: y(v), r: 5, fill: COL[lg], stroke: '#fff', 'stroke-width': 1 }, svg);
        bindMark(c, `<b>${MODEL[model]} · ${LANG[lg]} · λ = ${p.l}</b><br>${p.r.k} / ${p.r.n} ${kind} prompts refused = ${v.toFixed(2)}<br>Wilson 95% [${ci[0].toFixed(2)}, ${ci[1].toFixed(2)}]<br>${t === null ? 'recorded J1 label' : 'P(REFUSE) ≥ ' + t.toFixed(2)}`, `${MODEL[model]} ${LANG[lg]} at dose ${p.l}: ${p.r.k} of ${p.r.n} refused`);
      });
    });
    if (model === 'gemma_it') {
      const xr = W - m.r + 16; const rt = S('text', { x: xr, y: Ht - m.b + 16, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl' }, svg); rt.textContent = 'rand';
      [['en_bt', 'en'], ['sl_mt', 'sl']].forEach(([arm, lg], k) => {
        const r = drate(model, kind, arm, 'rand', t); if (!r) return; const v = r.k / r.n;
        const c = S('circle', { cx: xr + (k ? 5 : -5), cy: y(v), r: 5, fill: '#fff', stroke: COL[lg], 'stroke-width': 2 }, svg);
        bindMark(c, `<b>Gemma · ${LANG[lg]} · random-direction edits</b><br>${r.k} / ${r.n} ${kind} prompts refused = ${v.toFixed(2)}<br>three norm-matched random edits pooled`, `Gemma ${LANG[lg]} random-direction edits: ${r.k} of ${r.n} refused`);
        summ[model]['rand_' + lg] = r;
      });
    }
  });
  // takeaway at lambda = 1
  const at = (model, lg, l) => summ[model][lg].find(p => p.l === l).r;
  const g1e = at('gemma_it', 'en', 1), g1s = at('gemma_it', 'sl', 1), s1e = at('gams3_it', 'en', 1), s1s = at('gams3_it', 'sl', 1);
  const gaps = LAMS.map(l => { const e = at('gemma_it', 'en', l), s = at('gemma_it', 'sl', l); return s.k / s.n - e.k / e.n; });
  const pos = gaps.filter(g => g > 0).length;
  const rule = t === null ? 'Under the recorded labels' : `Refusing only when P(REFUSE) ≥ ${t.toFixed(2)}`;
  let tk = `${rule}, at λ = 1 Gemma refuses ${g1s.k}/${g1s.n} ${kind} prompts in Slovene and ${g1e.k}/${g1e.n} in English; GaMS3 refuses ${s1s.k}/${s1s.n} and ${s1e.k}/${s1e.n}. `;
  tk += `Gemma's Slovene rate is above its English rate at ${pos} of ${LAMS.length} doses (largest gap ${(Math.max(...gaps) * 100).toFixed(0)} points).`;
  if (kind === 'benign') { const e0 = at('gemma_it', 'en', 0), s0 = at('gemma_it', 'sl', 0); tk += ` On benign twins the unedited Gemma already refuses ${s0.k}/${s0.n} in Slovene against ${e0.k}/${e0.n} in English; the gap is widest before the edit.`; }
  $('#tk-dose').textContent = tk;
}
$$('input[name="ds-kind"]').forEach(e => e.addEventListener('change', drawDose));
$('#ds-argmax').addEventListener('change', drawDose);
$('#ds-t').addEventListener('input', drawDose);
onResize($('#c-dose-gemma_it'), drawDose);

// ======================================================= ROBUSTNESS
const SLICES = [
  { key: 'primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT', name: 'Primary: Slovene MT vs English back-translation', items: ITEMS, coding: 'R', idx: PRIMARY },
  { key: 'SLMT_vs_ENorig', name: 'Original English as the English arm', items: ITEMS, coding: 'R', idx: [4, 1, 5, 3] },
  { key: 'mt_fragile_dropped', name: 'MT-fragile items dropped', items: ITEMS.filter(i => !i[4]), coding: 'R', idx: PRIMARY },
  { key: 'orbench_only', name: 'OR-Bench items only', items: ITEMS.filter(i => i[2] !== 'X'), coding: 'R', idx: PRIMARY },
  { key: 'xstest_only', name: 'XSTest items only', items: ITEMS.filter(i => i[2] === 'X'), coding: 'R', idx: PRIMARY },
  { key: 'primary_Rp', name: 'PARTIAL counted as refusal', items: ITEMS, coding: 'RP', idx: PRIMARY },
  { key: 'ENBT_vs_ENorig_MTnoise', name: 'Placebo: back-translation vs original English (no language change)', items: ITEMS, coding: 'R', idx: [4, 0, 5, 2] }
];
SLICES.forEach(s => { const r = sdt(s.items, s.coding, s.idx); s.c = r.didc; s.d = r.didd; s.n = r.n; const rec = SDT.recorded[s.key]; s.cci = rec.DiD_c_ci95; s.dci = rec.DiD_d_ci95; s.rc = rec.DiD_c; s.rd = rec.DiD_d; });
let own = null;
function drawRobust() {
  const par = radio('rb-par'), onlyFail = $('#rb-fail').checked;
  const P = SLICES[0];
  let rows = SLICES.map(s => ({ name: s.name, v: s[par], ci: s[par + 'ci'], rec: s['r' + par], n: s.n, key: s.key }));
  if (own) rows.push({ name: own.name, v: own[par], ci: own[par + 'ci'], n: own.n, key: 'own', own: true });
  const breaks = r => !r.ci ? false : (r.ci[0] <= 0 && r.ci[1] >= 0) || Math.sign(r.v) !== Math.sign(P[par]) && r.key !== 'primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT';
  if (onlyFail) rows = rows.filter(r => r.key === 'primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT' || breaks(r));
  const box = $('#c-robust'); box.innerHTML = '';
  const W = Math.max(300, box.clientWidth), narrow = W < 620, rh = narrow ? 58 : 38, m = { l: narrow ? 12 : 330, r: 16, t: 14, b: 40 }, Ht = m.t + rows.length * rh + m.b;
  const svg = S('svg', { viewBox: `0 0 ${W} ${Ht}`, role: 'group', 'aria-label': 'Difference-in-differences by slice' }, box);
  const all = rows.flatMap(r => r.ci ? [r.ci[0], r.ci[1], r.v] : [r.v]); const lo = Math.min(-0.8, ...all) - 0.05, hi = Math.max(0.9, ...all) + 0.05;
  const x = v => m.l + (v - lo) / (hi - lo) * (W - m.l - m.r);
  const g = S('g', { class: 'axis' }, svg);
  for (let t = Math.ceil(lo * 4) / 4; t <= hi; t += 0.25) { const xx = x(t); S('line', { x1: xx, x2: xx, y1: m.t, y2: Ht - m.b, stroke: Math.abs(t) < 1e-9 ? '#6b717c' : COL.grid, 'stroke-dasharray': Math.abs(t) < 1e-9 ? '4 3' : '' }, g); const tx = S('text', { x: xx, y: Ht - m.b + 16, 'text-anchor': 'middle' }, g); tx.textContent = f(t, 2); }
  const xl = S('text', { x: (m.l + W - m.r) / 2, y: Ht - 6, 'text-anchor': 'middle', class: 'lbl' }, svg); xl.textContent = (par === 'c' ? 'DiD on criterion c' : 'DiD on sensitivity d′') + ' (z units); dashed line = 0';
  rows.forEach((r, i) => {
    const yy = m.t + i * rh + (narrow ? 36 : rh / 2);
    const lt = S('text', narrow ? { x: m.l, y: yy - 16, class: 'lbl', fill: '#1b1d21' } : { x: m.l - 10, y: yy + 4, 'text-anchor': 'end', class: 'lbl', fill: '#1b1d21' }, svg);
    lt.textContent = r.name + (r.own ? ' (your slice)' : ''); if (r.key === 'primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT' || r.own) lt.setAttribute('font-weight', 700);
    const bad = breaks(r);
    const colr = r.own ? '#0b5cad' : bad ? '#b3261e' : (par === 'c' ? '#d55e00' : '#4a4f58');
    if (r.ci) S('line', { x1: x(r.ci[0]), x2: x(r.ci[1]), y1: yy, y2: yy, stroke: colr, 'stroke-width': 2.5, 'stroke-linecap': 'round' }, svg);
    const dot = S('circle', { cx: x(r.v), cy: yy, r: 6.5, fill: colr, stroke: '#fff', 'stroke-width': 1.5 }, svg);
    const vt = S('text', { x: x(r.ci ? r.ci[1] : r.v) + 10, y: yy + 4, class: 'lbl' }, svg); vt.textContent = fs(r.v, 2); if (x(r.ci ? r.ci[1] : r.v) + 44 > W) { vt.setAttribute('x', x(r.ci ? r.ci[0] : r.v) - 10); vt.setAttribute('text-anchor', 'end'); }
    bindMark(dot, `<b>${esc(r.name)}</b><br>${par === 'c' ? 'DiD_c' : 'DiD_d′'} = ${fs(r.v, 3)} (recomputed here${r.rec !== undefined ? '; recorded ' + fs(r.rec, 3) : ''})<br>${r.ci ? '95% CI [' + f(r.ci[0], 2) + ', ' + f(r.ci[1], 2) + ']' + (r.own ? ' from your bootstrap' : ' recorded') : 'no interval yet: run the bootstrap'}<br>${r.n} items`, `${r.name}: ${fs(r.v, 3)}${r.ci ? ', 95% interval ' + f(r.ci[0], 2) + ' to ' + f(r.ci[1], 2) : ''}`);
  });
  const failing = rows.filter(r => r.key !== 'primary_SLMT_vs_ENBT' && breaks(r));
  const tk = par === 'c' ? `The primary criterion shift is ${fs(P.c, 2)}. ${failing.length ? 'It fails on ' + failing.map(r => r.name.charAt(0).toLowerCase() + r.name.slice(1) + ' (' + fs(r.v, 2) + ')').join('; ') + '.' : 'Every slice shown keeps an interval above zero.'} The OR-Bench items carry it, and recoding PARTIAL answers as refusals reverses its sign.`
    : `Sensitivity barely moves: the primary DiD on d′ is ${fs(P.d, 3)}${failing.length ? ', and ' + failing.length + ' of the slices shown have an interval spanning zero' : ''}. Whatever changes across slices, the models do not diverge in telling harmful from benign items.`;
  $('#tk-robust').textContent = tk;
}
$$('input[name="rb-par"]').forEach(e => e.addEventListener('change', drawRobust));
$('#rb-fail').addEventListener('change', drawRobust);
onResize($('#c-robust'), drawRobust);

function ownSlice() {
  const cmin = Number($('#own-c').value), cod = radio('own-cod'), src = $('#own-src').value;
  $('#own-cv').textContent = cmin;
  const its = ITEMS.filter(i => i[3] >= cmin).filter(srcFilter(src)); const r = sdt(its, cod);
  const name = `chrF ≥ ${cmin}, ${cod === 'R' ? 'REFUSE' : 'REFUSE+PARTIAL'}, ${src === 'all' ? 'all sources' : src === 'X' ? 'XSTest' : 'OR-Bench'}`;
  own = { name: name, c: r.didc, d: r.didd, n: r.n, its: its, cod: cod };
  $('#own-out').textContent = `${r.n} items kept (${r.ns} safe, ${r.nh} harmful). DiD_c = ${fs(r.didc, 3)}, DiD_d′ = ${fs(r.didd, 3)}. Gemma false alarms ${r.cells[0].fk}/${r.cells[0].fn} English vs ${r.cells[1].fk}/${r.cells[1].fn} Slovene. Press "Run bootstrap" for an interval.`;
  drawRobust();
}
$('#own-c').addEventListener('input', ownSlice);
$$('input[name="own-cod"]').forEach(e => e.addEventListener('change', ownSlice));
$('#own-src').addEventListener('change', ownSlice);
$('#own-boot').addEventListener('click', () => {
  const btn = $('#own-boot'); btn.disabled = true; btn.textContent = 'Resampling…';
  setTimeout(() => {
    const b = bootstrap(own.its, own.cod, PRIMARY, 2000, 20260924); own.cci = b.c; own.dci = b.d;
    $('#own-out').textContent = `${own.n} items kept. DiD_c = ${fs(own.c, 3)} [${f(b.c[0], 2)}, ${f(b.c[1], 2)}]; DiD_d′ = ${fs(own.d, 3)} [${f(b.d[0], 2)}, ${f(b.d[1], 2)}] from 2,000 stratified resamples (seed 20260924). ${b.c[0] > 0 ? 'The criterion interval stays above zero.' : 'The criterion interval reaches zero or below.'}`;
    drawRobust(); btn.disabled = false; btn.textContent = 'Run bootstrap';
  }, 20);
});

// ======================================================= NAV
const links = $$('nav.sec a'); const secs = links.map(a => document.querySelector(a.getAttribute('href')));
function setNav() { const yy = window.scrollY + 90; let cur = 0; secs.forEach((s, i) => { if (s.offsetTop <= yy) cur = i; }); if (window.innerHeight + window.scrollY >= document.body.scrollHeight - 4) cur = secs.length - 1; links.forEach((a, i) => a.setAttribute('aria-current', i === cur ? 'true' : 'false')); }

```
I built `interactive.html` (1.15 MB, a single file with no external resources) in the paper folder. Every chart on it is drawn in the browser from the run's recorded per-item outputs. I tested it in headless Chromium at 360, 390 and 1440 px: every control works, the console shows no errors, the page never scrolls sideways, and term definitions stay open after a real click.

**What the page shows:**
- **The finding:** refusal rates for each model and language, switchable between safe items (false alarms) and harmful items (hits) and filterable by item source. Beside them are a criterion plot and a d′/c table. The page recomputes the statistics from Experiment 5's 1,442 × 4 recorded labels and gets exactly what the artifact recorded: DiD<sub>c</sub> +0.522445 and DiD<sub>d′</sub> −0.002974.
- **How it works:** a 7-stage stepper that follows one real XSTest item, the "mangos' religious beliefs" prompt. Gemma answers it in English and refuses it in Slovene; GaMS3 answers in both languages.
- **Evidence:**
  - An item browser over 580 items: every item where Gemma's refusal differs between the two languages, plus a seeded random sample of 120 others. It is filterable and shows each prompt beside the four replies and their labels.
  - The prompt-language × reply-language grid from Experiment 14, with the unedited model as a baseline in each cell and the random-direction control.
- **Try it:** the Experiment 9 dose curves, with a slider that re-decides every reply using a threshold on the judge's recorded P(REFUSE).
- **Where it fails:** seven robustness slices plotted against their recorded confidence intervals. Two of them break the shift: XSTest items only (+0.10) and counting PARTIAL answers as refusals (−0.31). There is also a build-your-own-slice panel that runs a bootstrap in the browser.

**Things you should know:**
- **Possible error in the paper:** the Method section says the Slovene prompts for this experiment were translated with NLLB. The Experiment 5 records say they were translated by Gemini, with a gpt-4.1-mini back-translation. NLLB was used only for an XSTest-only arm and in Experiments 9 and 14. The page follows the records and notes the discrepancy; `paper.tex` may need correcting.
- **A challenge to the title:** on Experiment 9's benign twin prompts, Gemma's extra Slovene false refusals are largest before the edit (39/150 vs 12/150) and narrow as the dose increases. The page's takeaway says this plainly.
- **No paper figures on the page:** all three are data plots, so the page draws them live instead. The PNGs were already in `figures/`, so nothing needed rendering.
- **Other files:** `index.html` already linked to `interactive.html` in its hero and footer with the right label, so I left it unchanged. I added one line to `README.md` listing the new page, and wrote `.terminal_claude_agent_struct_out.json`.

The extraction, build and test scripts are in my scratchpad, outside the published folder.
